They are organized into categories and have inventory tracked across warehouses. **Key Attributes**: - Unique SKU code - Human-readable product name - Unit price in base currency (EUR) - Active/inactive status - Belongs to exactly one Category **Business Rules**: - Must belong to a valid category before being sold - Prices can change daily based on market conditions - Inactive products cannot be ordered but remain for historical reference **Synonyms**: item, article, goods, merchandise, SKU **Related Concepts**: Category, Inventory, OrderLineItem **Examples**: - "Wireless Bluetooth Headphones - Black" (SKU: ELE-001234) - "Cotton T-Shirt - Medium, Blue" (SKU: CLO-002345) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── SALES ORDER ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── **Definition**: A formal transaction document recording the agreement between the platform and a Customer to supply Products. **Business Context**: Orders are created when customers complete checkout. They track the customer, items, payment status, and delivery information. **Key Attributes**: - Unique Order ID - References exactly one Customer - Order date when transaction was initiated - Total monetary value - Status: PENDING, CONFIRMED, SHIPPED, DELIVERED, CANCELLED - Must contain at least one Order Line Item **Business Rules**: - Cannot be shipped until payment is confirmed - Can only be cancelled if not yet shipped - Status changes are logged for audit purposes **Synonyms**: order, purchase order, transaction, customer order **Related Concepts**: Customer, OrderLineItem, CustomerAddress **Examples**: - Order #12345 for Customer #10001 containing 3 items - Order #12346 with status "DELIVERED" from last week ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ORDER LINE ITEM ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── **Definition**: A single line within a Sales Order specifying a Product, quantity, and unit price at time of purchase. **Business Context**: Line items break down orders into individual product purchases. Each captures the price at the moment of ordering. **Key Attributes**: - Unique line identifier - References exactly one Product - Quantity of units ordered - Unit price at time of order (historical, not current) - Extended amount = quantity × unit price

Multiple payment methods are supported. **Key Attributes**: - Unique Payment ID - References exactly one Sales Order - Payment method (credit card, PayPal, bank transfer) - Payment amount - Confirmation timestamp - Status: PENDING, CONFIRMED, FAILED, REFUNDED **Business Rules**: - Payment must be confirmed before order ships - Refunds create new payment records with negative amounts - Multiple payment attempts can exist for one order **Synonyms**: transaction, payment transaction **Related Concepts**: SalesOrder **Examples**: - Credit card payment of €156.48 for Order #12345 - PayPal payment of €45.00 for Order #12346 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── SHIPMENT ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── **Definition**: The physical delivery of Products from a Warehouse to a Customer's delivery address. **Business Context**: Shipments represent the logistics side of order fulfillment. They track what items were sent, when, and to whom. **Key Attributes**: - Unique Shipment ID - References exactly one Sales Order - Source Warehouse - Destination Customer Address - Shipped timestamp - Tracking number - Status: PREPARING, SHIPPED, IN_TRANSIT, DELIVERED **Business Rules**: - Can only be created for confirmed orders with payment - One order may have multiple partial shipments - Delivery address must belong to the order's customer **Synonyms**: delivery, package, consignment **Related Concepts**: SalesOrder, Warehouse, CustomerAddress, Inventory **Examples**: - Shipment #S-001 containing 2 items from Warehouse WH-EU-01 - Shipment #S-002 with tracking number "1Z999AA1" for Order #12347 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── KEY RELATIONSHIP SUMMARY ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Customer Relationships: - A Customer places zero or more Sales Orders - A Customer has one or more Customer Addresses (not in simplified schema) Product Relationships: - A Product belongs to exactly one Category - A Product appears on zero or more Order Line Items Sales Order Relationships: - A Sales Order is placed by exactly one Customer - A Sales Order has one or more Order Line Items - A Sales Order has one or more Payments - A Sales Order has one or more Shipments Order Line Item Relationships: - An Order Line Item is part of exactly one Sales Order - An Order Line Item references exactly one Product Payment Relationships: - A Payment is for exactly one Sales Order
